text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- S E R B I A -
NASA BORBA
- The EU is dissatisfied with the slow fulfillment of EU and international community expectations by Belgrade, Zagreb and Sarajevo.
- The Serb-Kosovo Albanian dialogue will be held on June 23 in Montenegro's coastal town of Ulcinj instead of in Pec.
- Yugoslavia will resume talks with the London Club of creditor banks in London on June 23 and 24.
- Striking medics say they cannot return to work as instructed by government because they do not have the necessary supplies they need to work with.
- We will enter a phase of even greater social upheavals in autumn, says president of the Confederation of Autonomous Trade Unions of Yugoslavia (SSSJ) Dragan Radulovic.
- Montenegrin Trade Union to ask for early republican and federal elections because those elected last year did not justify the confidence given them.
- Participants of the Serb-Serb dialogue on Kosovo agreed to form an expert group which would draft a proposal for resolving the problem of Serb-Kosovo Albanian relations.
- After two years of boycott over lack of live coverage the Democratic Party considers returning to the republican parliament because of important decisions expected to be made.
- New draft law on foreign trade proposes channeling all deals through the National Bank of Yugoslavia and not the authorised bank as done earlier, shows aim to go towards greater centralisation.
- According to a poll conducted by Markplan agency on 2280 pollees, furniture firm Simpo, confectionary factory Soko Stark and drug factory ICN Galenika top the list of best Yugoslav firms.
POLITIKA
- Serbian parliament session scheduled for June 30, to discuss among other laws the law on local government.
- Yugoslav Foreign Minister Milan Milutinovic is visiting Rome at the invitation of his Italian counterpart Lamberto Dini; the visit comes within the scope of regular contacts.
- Serbia plans to finance large infrastructure projects but only from real sources, says deputy president of the Serbian Chamber of Commerce Momir Pavlicevic.
- The Yugoslav government submits bill on customs tariffs to parliament which is aimed at protecting domestic production.
- We cannot improve our trade balance by reducing imports of needed semi-manufactured goods but by increasing exports, said Yugoslav Foreign Minister Borislav Vukovic.
- Serbian Chamber of commerce today holds final discussion on the republic's privatisation law which is expected to start being implemented in November.
- The Montenegrin government is for the Yugoslav federation, says Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
BORBA
- Cigarette smuggling is blocking domestic cigarette production, Vranje Tobacco Industry DIV reduced its production to only 30 percent because of inflated stocks due to street cigarette sales.
- M O N T E N E G R O -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic to address the republic's parliament on Thursday, Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic also expected to speak.

- President Bulatovic said in Ulcinj he did not betray Montenegro in response to accusations. Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic said equality was not on sale and that Yugoslavia should return to the international community as soon as possible.

- Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic visited Berane on Wednesday rejecting accusations the government was favouring the south of the country. He said 67 percent of the funds allocated by the Directorate for Public Works were given to the north, while the government granted $2 million to Berane companies and $500,000 for social welfare programmes.
- Local branches of ruling DPS of Herceg Novi, Pluzine and Mojkovac are against holding of the extraordinary party congress.

- Montenegro airlines will have the first Belgrade-Podgorica commercial flight on Thursday. The airline will establish a regular service between the two cities from mid-July. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
